title: Weather as the itinerary
standfirst: Where the word Inntinn comes from, and a country that rewards working with the forecast rather than against it.

blocks.heading: An estate, taken whole
paras: Scotland is at its best when a group has the run of a place and no fixed plan for the week.
A sporting estate taken whole gives a family the house, the staff, the water and the hill, and lets each morning decide what the day is.

blocks.heading: The islands, by boat
blocks.caption: Island days held loosely against the forecast.
paras: The Hebrides are a different country again, and the crossings are entirely at the weather's discretion.
We hold boat days as options rather than fixtures, and we keep a second plan for every one of them.

blocks.heading: Stalking, fishing, and the ghillie
blocks.caption: The ghillie makes the week, not the house.
paras: On any estate the person who determines the quality of the week is the ghillie or the stalker, not the architecture.
We book the people before the property, and we say so when an estate's are not up to standard.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: May to September for the islands and the light. October for stalking and for the colour.
Real, and worst in still weather from June to August on the west coast. The east coast and a breeze solve most of it.

items.q: Is an estate only for shooting?
a: No. Most of the estates we use are taken by families who never pick up a rod or a rifle and simply want the house and the hill.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
